Jonas / Marissa — answering the metering portion. TL;DR: we meter per request but apply a small billing quantum and give cache credits for repeated KV references. Details and examples below. Attaching a CSV with worked examples (metering_examples.csv).

How we meter (high level):
- Metering scope: each API call is evaluated independently for billed tokens (input tokens + generated tokens). We do not bill "per session" as a separate recurring unit.
- Quantum: for generation requests we round the total tokens billed for that request up to the next 16-token quantum. For short calls, that quantum is the primary source of rounding noise.
- Streaming: streaming responses are still billed at the request boundary; internal stream chunking does not create extra billing events.
- Cache behavior: we maintain a KV prefix cache. When a token sequence is served entirely from the cache (no recomputation), the request is eligible for a cache credit that reduces the billed input tokens for that request by the cached token count up to a configurable cap (default 8k). However, cached tokens still count when they are newly introduced into the model context (first time seen).
- Minimums/floors: we do not bill idle sessions, but we do enforce a per-request floor (the quantum above). We also offer a seat/session bundle option that can include a nominal monthly per-session floor for unlimited short interactions — this is optional and set via contract.

Worked examples (rounded math):
1) Short burst
- Client sends request with 450 input tokens and asks for up to 200 generated tokens. Raw total = 650 tokens.
- Apply 16-token quantum: 650 -> round up to 656 (650 / 16 = 40.625 -> 41 * 16 = 656).
- Billed tokens = 656.

2) Long persistent session (cache hit case)
- First turn: 6,200 input tokens (context injection) + 300 generation = 6,500 -> rounded to 6,512 -> billed 6,512.
- Later turn where 3,000 of those input tokens are served from KV cache and not new:
  - Raw total = 3,000 input (of which 3,000 are cached) + 150 generation = 3,150.
  - Apply cache credit: subtract 3,000 cached tokens (up to cap) -> adjusted billable tokens = 150.
  - Apply quantum: 150 -> rounded up to 160.
  - Billed tokens = 160.

Notes and caveats:
- Cache credits are not retroactive: once a token is billed as "new" it won't be credited later. Credits apply only when the cache serves tokens instead of recomputing them.
- Very long single requests (where input + output > 100k tokens) require a specialized path and a different metering regime; we'll flag those cases and treat them as negotiated unit pricing.

If you want, I can produce the same examples using Acme's sample traffic (I used the CSV above to show the mapping).

Commercial options we can offer for the pilot / procurement:
- Pilot concession: waive any per-session contractual minimums for the first 90 days of a paid pilot. This only affects the optional per-session floor in Dedicated-seat bundles; it does not change per-request metering.
- Usage discount: standard committed usage tiers apply. For deals like this we typically propose a stepped discount: 7% at $25k/mo+, 12% at $75k/mo+, 18% at $200k/mo+. We can move to custom pricing if ACME wants a larger commit.
- Billing smoothing: if the customer prefers we can aggregate daily requests into a consolidated daily bill (helps with bursty traffic). That aggregation does not change the per-request quantum rounding — it only reduces invoice line-item noise.

Emma — thanks for the sample. Putting Ben and Marissa's input into one place so procurement has what it needs. See short answers first, then attached worked examples and a draft SOW.

Short answers:
- Rounding/quantum: we bill per API call and round each call up to the next 16-token quantum. That is the only implicit minimum most customers see.
- Cache handling: tokens served from our KV cache are eligible for cache credits and will generally NOT be billed again when referenced later (subject to the cache cap and the initial-first-seen rule). For your traffic we saw large first-turn costs but subsequent turns had very favorable crediting.
- Idle sessions: we do not bill for "idle time." Charges come from API calls only. The only session-level floor is an optional contract feature, which Marissa can waive for the pilot.
